cases.requirement: Appending one record to an empty ledger produces exactly one entry at sequence 0.
A successful append adds its entry only at the existing ledger tail.
A successful append preserves every pre-existing ledger entry unchanged.
Successful appends assign unique per-ledger sequences in strictly increasing order.
A snapshot lists the current ledger in strictly increasing gap-free sequence order beginning at 0.
One successful append invocation creates exactly one new ledger occurrence.
Two successful invocations with structurally equal record payloads remain two distinct ledger occurrences with different sequences.
M5-001 exposes no portable update operation capable of rewriting an existing sequence.
M5-001 exposes no portable replace operation capable of replacing an existing ledger entry.
M5-001 exposes no portable delete operation capable of removing an existing ledger entry.
M5-001 exposes no portable truncate or clear operation capable of shortening ledger history.
M5-001 exposes no portable insert or move operation capable of reordering existing history.
APPENDED is returned only when the invocation authoritatively produced exactly one new immutable tail entry.
NOT_APPENDED authoritatively means the failed invocation produced no new ledger entry.
An append failure proven not to have published leaves that invocation's ledger contribution absent rather than partially visible.
A failure whose publication state cannot be proven is represented as INDETERMINATE rather than false APPENDED or NOT_APPENDED authority.
INDETERMINATE is not automatically retried by the M5-001 contract and does not imply exactly-once delivery.
The store never reports APPENDED for a record it silently drops before its declared publication boundary.
Mutating caller-owned input after APPENDED cannot change the already stored logical entry.
Mutating a value obtained from snapshot observation cannot rewrite already stored ledger state.
Two overlapping successful appends to one ledger are published in one total order with no duplicate sequence.
A successful append observed before another append begins has a lower sequence than the later successful append.
Sequence and ordering authority are scoped to one ledger and do not create a global cross-ledger order.
An append failure in one ledger does not mutate another ledger as hidden compensation.
M5-001 does not define canonical JSON or require a canonical byte representation for records.
cases.evidence: Spec 0053 sections 1, 3.1 and 15; M5-002 owns canonical JSON.

cases.requirement: M5-001 does not compute or require record digests, previous-record digests, or hash chains.
